Help.title: Help
Help.subtitle: How Velto works and what each section is for — a guide in plain language.

intro.title: What is Velto?
intro.intro: Velto is a sales management system for distributors. Everything — from an order taken on an agent's phone to the warehouse, the cash desk and the reports — is handled in one place. Instead of paper notebooks, scattered Excel files and phone agreements, it all lives in the system.

groups.heading: What the system solves
items: Which customer owes how much, and since when — visible at a glance.
Which shop the agent visited and how many orders they took — tracked through the day.
How much stock you have and how much is reserved for orders — calculated automatically.
Every sum a cashier accepts is recorded against the invoice it pays off.

groups.heading: Key terms
items: Customer — the company or entrepreneur you sell to. One customer can have several outlets.
Outlet — a customer's specific shop with its address. Routes are built from outlets.
Order — the list of products a customer asked for, and its total.
Invoice — the document to be paid, created once the order is delivered. Debt is counted from it.
Payment — money received from a customer. It is allocated to invoices and reduces the debt.
Route — the list of outlets an agent visits on a given weekday.

roles.title: Who does what
roles.intro: Each employee only sees the sections their job needs. The menu depends on your role — a missing section is not an error.

items: Admin — sees and changes everything: staff, settings, prices, reports.
Director — owns sales: orders, customers, agents, routes and reports.
Warehouse — receives goods, keeps stock levels, picks and ships orders.
Cashier — opens a shift, accepts money from customers, closes the shift at the end of the day.
Accountant — works with payments, receivables and financial reports.
Agent — works from the Telegram app on their phone: visits the customer, takes the order, collects money.

start.title: Where to start
start.intro: The system arrives empty. Fill it in this order — each step builds on the one before it, so nothing gets tangled.

groups.heading: Step by step
items: Settings — enter the company name, phone, address, currency and time zone.
Users — add your staff and give each a role. The password is shown once; hand it to the employee yourself.
Products — enter what you sell: name, code, price, packaging.
Stock — use the "Receive" button to enter the quantities you actually have.
Customers — add your shops and give each one an outlet.
Routes — decide which agent visits which outlets on which day.

groups.heading: Tip
items: Don't try to enter everything at once. Start with 10–20 products and 5–10 customers, and run a single order all the way through.
That gives you a feel for how the system works and makes it easier to explain to your staff.

flow.title: From order to money: the daily cycle
flow.intro: Every order follows the same path. The status tells you which stage an order is at right now.

groups.heading: Stages
items: Submitted — the agent or an operator entered the order; it is waiting for review.
Confirmed — the order is accepted and the goods are reserved in the warehouse for that customer.
Delivered — the goods were handed over. At that moment stock goes down and an invoice is created.
Closed — the invoice is fully paid and the order is finished.
Cancelled — the order fell through; the reserved goods are released.

groups.heading: Who works at each stage
items: The agent or an operator creates the order.
The director or admin confirms it.
The warehouse picks the goods and marks the order delivered.
The cashier takes the money, and once the debt is cleared the order is closed.

dashboard.title: Home page
dashboard.intro: A short picture of the day. Opening the page shows you today's state right away.

items: Today's turnover and order count — compared with yesterday.
Money collected — what came into the cash desk today.
Overdue debt — amounts past their payment deadline. If this number grows, collection needs more attention.
The last 30 days chart — shows whether sales are rising or falling.
Agents today — who made how many visits and took how many orders.
Largest debtors — who to deal with first.

orders.title: Orders
orders.intro: All orders live here. The list can be filtered by status or customer.

groups.heading: Creating an order
items: Press "New order".
Search for and pick the customer; specify the outlet if needed.
Use "Add line" to enter the product, packaging and quantity; add a discount if needed.
Next to each product you see the free stock left — don't write more than that.
Save. The order appears in the list with the "Submitted" status.

groups.heading: Buttons on the order card
items: "Confirm" — reserves the goods for this customer.
"Mark delivered" — reduces stock and creates the invoice.
"Close" — finishes the order once it is fully paid.
"Cancel" — you can record a reason; the reserved goods are released.

customers.title: Customers
customers.intro: Your customer base: who you work with, on what terms they buy, and how much they owe.

groups.heading: When adding a customer
items: Code — the customer's internal number; it must be unique.
Payment term (days) — how many days the customer has to pay an invoice. Past that, the debt is marked overdue.
Price list — which prices apply to this customer.
Outlet — the customer's shop. If there are several, the rest can be added later.

groups.heading: Good to know
items: If a customer with the same phone or a similar name already exists, the system warns you — to prevent duplicates.
A customer can be blocked: no new orders can then be written for them.
A customer with outstanding debt cannot be deleted.
For a deleted customer, the order and payment history is kept.

products.title: Products
products.intro: The list of what you sell. Both orders and stock rely on it.

items: SKU — the product's internal code; it is unique.
Base unit — what you count in: pieces, kg or litres.
Packagings — how many pieces are in one box. An agent can count in boxes while the warehouse counts in pieces.
Price — the price for one base unit.
Opening stock — while adding a product you can enter the quantity you already have.
Image — helps the agent find the product faster on their phone.
A product you no longer sell can be made "inactive" instead of deleted.

stock.title: Stock
stock.intro: What is in the warehouse. Each product shows three numbers, and they mean different things.

groups.heading: What the numbers mean
items: On hand — the quantity physically sitting in the warehouse.
Reserved — the quantity held for confirmed orders.
Available — what can still be sold on new orders: on hand minus reserved.

groups.heading: Receiving goods
items: Use "Receive" and enter the product, quantity and reason.
Stock is never erased by hand — every movement is recorded, so it is always clear who entered what and when.
If a stock count finds a discrepancy, it is corrected with a receipt here too.

cash.title: Cash desk and payments
cash.intro: Taking money from customers. A cash shift must be open before any payment can be accepted.

groups.heading: The daily routine
items: At the start of the day press "Open shift" and enter the opening amount in the drawer.
During the day accept money through "New payment".
At the end of the day press "Close shift" and enter the actual amount in the drawer. The system compares it with what was collected.

groups.heading: Allocating a payment
items: Automatic (FIFO) — the money is applied starting from the oldest open invoice. This is the usual choice.
Manual — you decide exactly which invoice the customer is paying for.
Payment method: cash, card or bank transfer.
A saved payment is never deleted — a mistake is fixed with a new correcting entry.

suppliers.title: Suppliers
suppliers.intro: The companies that deliver goods to you.

items: You can add a supplier and assign a route to them.
Telegram link — you generate a link code and send it to the supplier; once they enter it in the bot, they start receiving order notifications.
A supplier you are not working with for now can be deactivated instead of deleted.

routes.title: Routes
routes.intro: A route is the list of outlets, in order, that one agent (or supplier) covers on a given weekday.

groups.heading: Building a route
items: Choose who it belongs to: an agent or a supplier.
Pick the weekday — for example, every Tuesday.
Add stops: search for the customer first, then choose their outlet.
Reorder with the arrows — the agent travels in exactly this sequence.

groups.heading: Why it matters
items: The agent sees the day's list on their phone and doesn't forget a shop.
Reports gain "route completion" — how many of the planned stops were actually visited.

agents.title: Agents
agents.intro: Your sales agents and today's results on one page.

items: Each agent shows today's visits, orders and turnover.
An agent is a user with the "Agent" role. Adding an agent means creating a new user.
If no route is assigned to an agent, they won't see a daily list on their phone.

reports.title: Reports
reports.intro: You pick a date range and the system does the maths. Tables can be exported to Excel.

groups.heading: Tabs
items: Overview — turnover, order count, average check, active and new customers, total debt.
Sales — daily turnover chart, a breakdown by agent, and the best-selling products.
Agent performance — visits, route completion, effective visits (those that ended in an order) and average check.
Receivables — debt grouped by age: current, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90 and 90+ days. The further right a column, the harder that money is to collect.

users.title: Users
users.intro: This is where staff are given access to the system.

items: The phone number is the login. The password is shown once when created; pass it to the employee yourself.
The role decides which sections the employee sees. One user can hold several roles.
When someone leaves, you don't have to delete them — deactivating is enough and keeps the history.
If an employee has records in the system, deleting them anonymises their data while the order and payment history stays in place.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.intro: The log of who did what, and when.

items: Logins, order confirmations, price changes, user creation and similar actions are recorded automatically.
These records cannot be edited or deleted — not even by an admin.
This is where you find the answer to "why did stock change?" or "who cancelled this order?".

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: The basic company details: name, legal name, phone, address, currency and time zone.

items: These details are used in documents and reports.
If the time zone is wrong, daily reports can land on the wrong day.
Changing them requires the right permission, and every change goes into the audit log.

miniapp.title: The app on the agent's phone
miniapp.intro: Sales agents don't use the web version — they work in the app inside Telegram.

items: The agent arrives at the shop, opens a visit and enters the order on the spot.
It works without internet: the data is stored on the phone and sent by itself once the connection is back.
That is why an order may show up in the web version a few minutes later — this is not a fault.
Data on the phone is stored encrypted: if the phone is lost, nobody else can read it.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: The situations that come up most often in daily work, and what causes them.

items: Some sections are missing from my menu — that depends on your role. An admin can add the role you need.
A product isn't in the list when creating an order — it hasn't been added yet, or it was made inactive.
A product can't be sold, available stock is zero — it is reserved for other confirmed orders, or the stock was never received.
A payment can't be added — the cash shift is probably not open. Open the shift first.
A customer's debt looks wrong — the invoice is only created once the order is delivered; an undelivered order is not counted as debt.
I forgot my password — use "Forgot password?" on the login page and a code is sent to your phone. If that fails, an admin can issue a new password.
Can data be exported to Excel — yes, list and report pages have an "Export to Excel" button.
How do I change the language — use the language button in the top right corner: Uzbek, Russian or English.

habits.title: Security and good habits
habits.intro: A few simple rules keep your data clean and trustworthy.

items: Never share your password — every action in the system is recorded under your name.
Give every employee their own account; don't use a shared one.
Close the cash shift at the end of the day so the daily report comes out right.
Count the warehouse physically once a week and correct any difference through "Receive".
Each company's data is stored separately — no other company can see yours.
